subject: sociology
title: Functionalism in Education: Parsons & Meritocracy
welcome_lead: Parsons sees school as the bridge — and the sorter.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology functionalism Parsons meritocracy secondary socialisation role allocation.
final_note: School translates families into society and grades us for our place.

concepts.def: Family — judged by who you are.
School — judged by what you do.
Sorting individuals into future jobs by ability.
Parsons — school links family and wider society.

walkthroughs.body_html: Parsons (1961): school is the focal socialising agency bridging family and society. Family judges children by particularistic standards ('my child') and ascribed status. School and wider society judge by universalistic standards (test scores) and achieved status.

Parsons argues modern society is a meritocracy — open contest for unequal rewards. Schools provide a level playing field and the most able rise to top jobs. Davis & Moore (1945): stratification is functional — high rewards motivate the talented to do difficult jobs.

Through exams and grades, school performs role allocation — matching talent to job. Society's most important jobs go to society's most able. Without this sorting, key roles would go unfilled or be done badly. Modern post-16 paths follow this logic.
